text:
Carla P: Heads-up — we're seeing a p99 jump for AcmePay after the runtime v5.2 canary rollout. p99 went ~380ms -> ~1.8s, p95 120ms -> 420ms. No increase in errors, but auth handshakes sometimes timeout.
Ben L: Which canary cohort/zone?
Carla P: Canary cohort C3 (EU-west), ~8% traffic. Deploy completed ~12:34 UTC.
deploy-bot: deploy finished: runtime v5.2 -> canary C3 @ 2025-11-03T12:34:12Z; kernel-selector=v2.1, kv-cache-mode=auto, batcher=continuous-v3.
Alice M: Any diffs in kernel selection or batching config vs prev?
Carla P: Kernel changed from v2.0 -> v2.1; batcher same name but new scheduler tweak rolled in.
Devon K: Can you paste tail logs for a slow trace? look for auth + kvcache misses.
Carla P: Paste of a slow request (p99 sample):
```
[12:45:02.112] request id=acme-req-42 start
[12:45:02.118] auth: start -> POST /auth/token -> 200 in 520ms
[12:45:02.640] kv-cache: miss (prefix=invoice-gen) -> backend fetch 1.1s
[12:45:03.752] runtime: kernel v2.1 selected, fallback path taken
[12:45:04.010] response sent total=1.898s
```
Devon K: kv-cache miss + backend fetch 1.1s is the big hit. Could be kvcache eviction/serialization change in v2.1.
Sasha R: Cross-check: do we see increased cold-kv misses for tenant-local caches or global store?
Carla P: Metric: acmepay.kv_cache.miss_rate 4.2% -> 21.7% after rollout (5m window).
Ben L: Repro strategy: 1) rollback canary to v5.1 for C3 and observe p95/p99; 2) if rollback recovers, bisect kernel scheduler change between v2.0/v2.1; 3) if not, look at auth front-end.
Alice M: Agreed. Also short-term mitigation: route AcmePay traffic to isolated path (dedicated kv-cache warm) or enable kv-cache sticky warmup for that tenant. Can we flip a feature flag?
Carla P: We have tenant warmup flag: `tenant_kvcache_prewarm=true` — can toggle per-tenant from console.
oncall: I'm toggling prewarm for AcmePay now.
support-bot: CS ticket #2457 (AcmePay) updated: P1 latency escalation, informing account team.
Devon K: If rollback needed, plan: rollback canary C3 -> v5.1, monitor p95/p99 for 5 minutes, if stable, rollback other canaries. Keep trace sampling at 100% for AcmePay during test.
Ben L: Carla — can you run `curl -H "x-tenant: acmepay" https://canary-eu-west.runtime.internal/health?trace=1` against a few pods and share `kvcache.stats`?
Carla P: Running now, will paste results in 2m. :eyes:
Alice M: Also capture kernel allocator metrics: `runtime.kernel.alloc.latency{version=\"v2.1\"}` and compare to v2.0.
Carla P: Quick results: `kvcache.stats` on slow pod -> hits: 78, misses: 22 (miss ratio 21.8%); previous stable pods show miss ratio ~4.5%.
Ben L: That's consistent. Patch hypothesis: v2.1 change serialized cache lookup under load causing backend calls to spike.
Sasha R: Ok if we can't hotfix quickly, proceed with rollback + warmup toggle. I'll start a minimal canary rollback runbook.
Carla P: Rolling back C3 to v5.1 now (triggered at 12:51 UTC). Will report p95/p99 in 5m.
(5m later)
Carla P: After rollback p99 back to ~320ms, p95 110ms. Miss rate down to 5.1%. Looks like kernel selector change is culprit. :thumbsup:
Ben L: Good. Next: bisect the v2.1 changes in test cluster to find offending commit. Devon to own.
Devon K: I'll run bisect against kernel commits between v2.0..v2.1 in test with kvcache load tests. ETA 6h.
Sasha R: I'll draft a short rollback postmortem + mitigation steps: avoid auto-rolling kernel-selector without staged kvcache load test, add a canary KV warmup check.
Carla P: CS notified, account manager looped in. Closing the immediate oncall bell.
Ben L: Nice quick detection/rollback. Follow-up: add a canary metric alert for sudden kv_cache.miss_rate deltas > +10% baseline.
Alice M: I'll create the alert and add to canary runbook.
Carla P: Thanks team — moving to postmortem.
notes: P1; AcmePay impacted; rollback to v5.1 recovered p99; suspected kernel-selector v2.1 kvcache serialization; actions: bisect, add alerts, tenant warmup flag.
